subject: Ocelot POC — benchmark targets, reserved GPUs, and burst plan
messages:
From: Sara Blake <sara@ocelot.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Gabe Turner <gabe.turner@ocelot.ai>
Date: 2027-11-30T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + next steps for POC

Hi Priyom —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Gabe and I spoke after and we want to move forward with a short 3-week POC to validate latency and cost numbers on our document-conversion workload. Quick summary of what we care about: 

- Throughput: 250 concurrent infer requests (avg doc length 800 tokens)
- 95th pctl latency target: <180ms per token generation step (end-to-end)
- Cost: target $/1000 tokens to be comparable to our current on-prem setup

We also want to validate the autoscaling behavior during synthetic spike tests and confirm what guaranteed reserved capacity looks like for week-of-peak testing. Can Redwood reserve GPUs for our scheduled peak window (week of Dec 13)?

Attachments: we exported a sample load profile and our infrastructure diagram (will attach after internal scrub).

Next steps from our side: share sample S3 bucket with docs and a short success-criteria spreadsheet. Are you able to propose an evaluation plan and the GPU reservation numbers for the POC?

Best,
Sara
Sara Blake
Head of ML Engineering
Ocelot Analytics

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Sara Blake <sara@ocelot.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-30T18:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + next steps for POC

Sara — thanks, this is clear and a good summary. Quick recap and a proposed plan below.

Recap of Ocelot objectives (we heard):
- Validate latency and tail behavior at ~250 concurrent sessions on avg doc length ~800 tokens
- Measure token-level cost and compare to on-prem baseline
- Test autoscaling and controlled burst for scheduled peak (week of Dec 13)

Proposed evaluation plan (3-week POC):
Week 0 (prep, access): exchange keys + populate test S3, baseline deployments
Week 1 (functional, smoke): run small-scale runs to validate model selection and prompt templates; collect baseline metrics
Week 2 (scale tests): ramp to 250 concurrent using continuous batching and KV caching; run synthetic spikes (2x, 3x) to exercise autoscaler
Week 3 (acceptance): run acceptance tests, economic analysis, data export, and final review

Success criteria (proposal):
- Functional: correct structured outputs for 95% of sampled documents (we'll use your labeled set)
- Performance: 95th pctl latency <= 200ms per generation call (we'll measure both prefix and streaming time)
- Cost: unit token cost <= 1.15x of your on-prem baseline (accounting for storage/egress)
- Scalability: autoscaler must recover to steady-state within 3 minutes after a 3x synthetic spike with <5% error-rate increase

Capacity / reservation recommendation: 
- Reservation: 8 x A40-equivalent GPUs reserved for week-of-peak (Dec 13–19) during the POC acceptance window
- Default POC environment: 3 x A40-equivalent running with continuous batching and prefix caching enabled (autoscale up to reserved when triggered)
- Burst plan: allow autoscaling to burst to the 8 reserved GPUs for up to 4 hours/day during week-of-peak; sustained bursts >4h trigger ops notification and gating

Ownership:
- Redwood: infra provisioning, model variant selection, telemetry hooks, runbook for spike tests (Marissa will own ops during tests)
- Ocelot: dataset, acceptance labels, test S3, and spike schedule (Sara/Gabe)

Attachments I'll send by EOD: a draft POC runbook (redwood_poc_runbook_v1.pdf) and a capacity sheet with hourly ramp assumptions (ocelot_poc_capacity_sheet.xlsx).

If that looks good we'll lock the reservation and send a short MSA addendum for reserved capacity and burst windows.

Thanks — I'll open a HubSpot POC record and share links.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
